summary: Bannock County, ID frame cabin from the 1930s; abandoned per two site histories, gone per the FFLA list; no source describes the site today.

facts.status_note: Site histories say abandoned; the FFLA Idaho list says gone; no source says the cabin was removed or destroyed

events.note: Frame cabin; the sources give only the 1930s

evidence.supports: 12 miles south of Pocatello, Bannock County, elevation 8,700 ft
section 34, township 8 South, range 25 East, Caribou-Targhee National Forest
coordinates 42.67748 and -112.34568; listed as ground structure, gone
site histories call the cabin abandoned
no present-day description; latest recorded status is abandoned
firelookout.com page titled as a cabin

corrections.why: All three site pages name the Caribou-Targhee National Forest

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The FFLA list says Gone; firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts say Abandoned. We use abandoned because no source says the cabin was removed or destroyed.

notes_for_editor: Elevation 8,700 ft is from firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts; it is not a facts key, so it appears only in the story. The brief's status gone comes from the FFLA list; the two site histories say abandoned, which is why the status is recorded as abandoned. Idaho Fire Lookouts says it has no documented staffing history, so staffing is left out. The Drive-Up label is the only access-related detail; no source says whether the site is public, so access is not set. Camp Taylor's Scout Mountain Forest Recreation Area history covers a campground near 6,500 ft and does not mention this lookout, so it is not used.
